personally, i do not like this game. it reminds me of the game Lunacid, but worse in almost every way. I understand that they are separate genres, but they both scratch that itch for me of retro game with swords. but i don't like this game. The combat feels like it was really easy so the damage the enemies do was artificially inflated, and the gameworld so far has been basically just 3d binding of issac done worse. it feels like a slog to play. also, the first boss moves randomly which is unpleasant, because it's either extremely easy to dodge if you're far away, or impossible to dodge or predict if you're close. the ring system (you have to experiment which finger to put a ring on, and also if you even want a ring at all; ex. the chaos ring is bad and if you put the bullet ring on your sword hand swinging your sword will fire a bullet) is cool, as well as the potion system (each potion you find has 2 things it smells like and they can eithe buff or debuff you for that run; the same smells can be good or bad depending on what they're paired with) to a lesser extent, but overall i do not like this game, and would refund it if i could

This game is, by design, trying to make you feel like you did something wrong. And keeps punishing you for doing it. The core gameplay is pretty similar to Binding of Isaac, with the combat out of Kings Field (buy way faster) and makes itself appart from most games by being weird with its visuals (the intro is sick, I really love that monkey wizard thing). And while I do love Kings Field, it was not for the combat. By making it faster, it is way too hard to read enemies and prepare for what is coming. Take the skeletons, for example. They attack you by giving a very quick and subtle stab as soon as they get in range. Seems to be simple enough, but enemies blend into the psychodelical backgrounds and you can't really see where you got hit. Upgrades are pretty significant, with rings and weapons that can really change the course of the game, but good luck trying to get one. By the time you got to your first upgrade, you will be probably dead, or very close to it. There are also permanent upgrades that you can buy, but the currency is very hard to come by. I've found 4 of them so far, one from the boss and three from chests. Can't forget about the spells. To cast a spell, you use arround 10% of your HP to use a symbol, and usually a spell is composed of four symbols. So you must spend a LOT of your HP to cast a single spell. But, how do you know what spells to cast? And how to cast them? You can either find a blood mirror, a structure that has a chance to spawn in one of the rooms that gives you the name of the spell and what symbols it takes to cast it. Or, you can just f- arround and find out. So far, I've found out 3 spells, one of them by accident, and 2 from blood mirrors. One of them is "cast demon". Was trying to play arround with the symbols, restarting runs to find out if I could make a spell work (remember, 10% HP for each symbol and you have to guess a combination of four), and I've killed myself summoning a demon. Pretty metal. Next time I summon it, I spent half of my HP, summon the demon to take care of enemies in a room, and... the demon kills me. So, next spell: summon golem. This time, it is more worth it. It does not attack me. It does decent damage too. I end up dying (not before the lil guy), so I save the spell for the boss. The first boss in the game uses a shield during its attacks so the golem can't hit him. And when the shield disappears, the golem just... does nothing. It doesn't help with anything, does not shoot, nothing. It can't even get aggro, since all of the boss's attacks are AoE. I've wasted 40% of my HP to summon a dude to watch me die. The next spell is called "summon food". I cast summon food. A turnip appears on the ground. The turnip does nothing. I think that this game is trying to follow old game design tropes by trying to make everything super hard and inaccessible, but I'm not sure if this is a good idea. Old games didn't have tutorials inside them because tutorials were simply not a thing yet. Not because they thought that reading trought a manual was better. Old games were insanely hard to pad out the limited content that you could put inside a tinty floppy disk or a cartridge, not because players liked it. I've managed to get to the second area, but after dying to a group of skeletons pushing me into an acid pit, I don't know if I want to play this anymore. I'll give it a go when the 1.0 update launches, but I can't really recommend this game right now.

95% of this game is perfect. The atmosphere, music, sound design, and art design are amazing, top notch even. It's a true shame that the combat in this game is so woefully underdeveloped despite being its core mechanic. If the developer would add a blocking mechanic to the weapons that actually functioned and worked and you could actually do in the game, this game would be perfect. I'm very surprised that this is the finished product, especially considering the depth of all other elements. The RNG is fantastic, the magic system is interesting and presents a true challenge, but the way these elements meld with the combat is extremely unsatisfying. You basically have to almost kill yourself to execute spells, and these spells are not game-breaking, they are simple things that you think would be useful but ultimately are handicaps to player progression. The game is simply too clunky in its current state and desperately needs a combat overhaul. I truly hope the developer does not abandon this project as it is extremely promising. I'm not gonna stop playing, I'm gonna continue to hone my skills or whatever, but it will feel like a losing game until the developer fixes the combat.

So even though this is a negative review, this game is still an interesting game and is worth a play or two. It just wasn't for me and might not be for people similar to me. Making this thumb down one that is hard to tank as I'm writing this review, even though being honest with myself, I wouldn't recommend this game. As interesting as the mechanics are and as impressive as this game is when it comes to lore, ambiance and mystery, the execution is not well done enough for me to wanna keep playing. Especially with a rogue like game like this one. There's a lot of things to enjoy like learning concepts and having conversation to unlock stuff. Understanding more some mechanics of the game like the potion system, and so on. But it feels very repetitive. It feels like every biome has a slight monster pull change and different texture and that's it. It feels like there should be different bosses variations for the same level but it never happens. And it feels dull at a point. The worst part about it is the fact that the discovery of the systems and the begining of the game does feel amazing. But after a while, some music are very harsh and repetitive and fatigues you. You know you have to beat the same boss again and again but with the very punishing nature of the game, one mistakes during the dungeons will kill you and if not that, discovering the boss' patern will! And by then, you'll have find many rings, a lot of weapons which the changes in stats don't really matter too much in game feel, and you'll have meet a lot of characters where as long as you don't unlock concepts, the conversation is still locked and so nothing progress. The one thing that really bothered me and shouldn't have was the forest level. I was curious, with how many stuff you need to discover in order to compelte the awake world, about what tricks the game would pull in order for me to get everything as it makes it seem like the game has a lot of content hidden deeper in the dungeons... But it's just the same thing over and over again without features to make it feel fresh. I know games are that, bit it truly feel that each dungeons is a reskin of the first one. With those square rooms and unorganic mazes. I know roguelikes/lites are like that. But a game like returnal will trick you and have such a compelling narative that you'll get a driving force forward. Same with the first Hades and the way it always one up itself with challenges or boss changes and dialogue... Everything is too static to be compelling and it makes me feel in the end that its a very good start to a pretty average roguelike. So ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sad

One of my favorite games, but I will say that it can be very difficult, and it gets a bit dull repeating the same section repeatedly. Other than that the vibes are entirely immaculate, and (almost) overwhelmingly dungeon crawler. I've never seen or experienced anything like it. I can smell the mold, and damp gore as if it were a scented candle actively burning in my room. The crunch and static options in the settings are amazing, but the crunching also applies to the text, which can be a little annoying, but there is a sweet spot. The static option has remained around the highest setting for my entire playthrough so far, it's awesome. I didn't get to go into many of the key games blind growing up (Minecraft, Undertale, etc.) however most of the mechanics stand to make it feel like I'm genuinely exploring, growing, and learning as if I was actually an amnesiac relearning something I've already done. The magic system seems entirely useless most of the time, and often isn't used (if at all for some). As such, all of the spells tend to be entirely situational (at least until you level up health and blood usage during spells). The most useful spells so far have been golems (unmatched), and cursed weapon. Summon food is cool too for camels and Kenneth. The potions are cool too, as it forces you to memorize what tends to be good, and what tends to be bad. Honestly, I really wish there was merch so I could show my love and appreciation to the game's creator without having to bootleg something myself (as the case with many other pieces of media).
